title: Interlock roadmap check-in and risk digest — 2026-11-03
content:
Purpose: quick cross-team interlock focused on roadmap alignment, top risks for the next 4 weeks, and decisions that need sponsor sign-off. This note captures highlights, decisions, and action items from the 2026-11-03 engineering leadership staff check-in.

Attendees: Maya Chen (chair), Ravi Kapoor, Lucia Alvarez, Benji O'Neill, Priya Nair, Samir Patel, Marisol Gomez (observability), Aaron Liu (serving-runtime), Chloe Park (private deployments), Jonah Reed (devex) — apologies: Dan Erickson.

Agenda:
- 5m: quick metrics snapshot
- 20m: roadmap alignment across platform, serving runtime, and private deployments
- 20m: top risks & mitigations (capacity, regressions, compliance)
- 10m: staffing and hiring impact to delivery
- 5m: actions & next steps

Metrics snapshot (last 7 days):
- Hosted API p50/p95 latency (text gen, 128 tok): 42ms / 210ms (p95 off a minor tail spike on 11/01)
- Error budget burn: 0.8% (month-to-date), healthy vs SLA but trending with a spike tied to an infra rollout
- Dedicated capacity utilization (prod pools): avg 72% across regions; two pools in us-west >90% during peak windows
- KV cache hit rate for popular models: 61% overall; smaller models performing at 75%
- Rollout success rate (canary -> 100%): 92% (3/4 recent rollouts saw auto-rollback on slow token generation)

Roadmap alignment highlights:
- Platform-engineering: finalizing autoscaler policy improvements (JIRA-4482) — target deploy to staging 11/10, prod 11/17. Main risk is scheduler churn during burst tests.
- Serving-runtime: kernel selection enhancement for grouped attention (PR #987) scheduled for beta on 11/12. Expected p95 latency improvement for long-context paths; needs focused regression test on tokenization edge cases.
- Private deployments: onboarding checklist v2 for customer-managed KMS and network policies is drafted; compliance team wants an audit preview by 11/18.
- Observability: new per-route token-cost breakdown dashboard prototype (internal link above) will be demoed to CS on 11/09. Retention plan for traces still pending decision.

Top risks and proposed mitigations:
1) Capacity hotspots in us-west (risk: customer throttles / degraded latency)
   - Observation: two dedicated pools hitting >90% at peak.
   - Mitigation: short-term: reroute low-priority batch work to regional spare capacity (DevOps runbook updated). Medium-term: increase reserved capacity by 10% for peak windows (finance approval required).
   - Owner: Ravi Kapoor; due: 2026-11-10 (reroute config), 2026-11-20 (capacity commit).

2) Regression risk from grouped-attention kernel change (risk: correctness/perf regressions for edge models)
   - Observation: earlier kernel swaps caused rare under-generation for a small set of tokenizers.
   - Mitigation: add focused tokenization regression suite and gate PRs behind it; expand canary phasing to 5% -> 25% -> 100% with staged telemetry hooks.
   - Owner: Aaron Liu; due: 2026-11-12 (test suite), 2026-11-16 (canary plan).

3) Compliance timeline for private deployments (risk: audit schedule compresses release window)
   - Observation: compliance asked for audit-ready artifacts by 11/18 which overlaps with private-deploy checklist rollout.
   - Mitigation: prioritize minimal audit artifacts (KMS key rotation policy, network topology doc, OB-logs retention proposal). Avoid sweeping feature merges that expand surface area before audit.
   - Owner: Chloe Park + Priya Nair; due: 2026-11-16 (artifact bundle).

Decisions made during meeting:
- Temporary freeze on non-blocker infra changes for the serving-runtime release window 11/10–11/18. Emergency exceptions require SRE and Platform VP approval. (Decision owner: Maya Chen)
- Approve targeted 10% reserved capacity uplift for us-west for Q4 peak; finance to review commit terms. (Ravi to lead finance sync)
- Require that any rollout touching kernel paths include tokenization regression sign-off. (Aaron to publish gating checklist in PR template)

Cross-team notes (short):
- Observability requested a short list of high-signal regression metrics for kernel changes (p95 token latency, token generation error rate, prefix-cache hit rate) — action assigned to Marisol.
- DevEx flagged 3 docs that need updates before the serving-runtime beta (quickstart, GPU sizing guide, example canary config). Jonah will convert doc issues into a sprint ticket.
- Private deployments: early adopter customer flagged a KMS UX gap; Chloe to triage with solutions eng and product.

Action items (owner — due):
- Ravi Kapoor — implement temporary reroute for low-priority batch jobs; 2026-11-10.
- Aaron Liu — publish tokenization regression suite + gate + PR-template update; 2026-11-12.
- Chloe Park & Priya Nair — assemble audit artifact bundle for compliance; 2026-11-16.
- Marisol Gomez — define 5 high-signal telemetry metrics and add to canary dashboard; 2026-11-09 (demo).
- Jonah Reed — create sprint tickets to update DevEx docs and track completion; 2026-11-08.
- Maya Chen — coordinate VP sign-off for temporary infra freeze exceptions; ongoing (checkpoint 2026-11-05).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Finance: confirm whether a Q4 reserved capacity uplift can be contracted on a 3-month trial; timeline for decision? (Ravi to escalate to Finance by 11/06)
- Security: does the compliance audit require a data localization addendum for the customer in EU/FR region? (Chloe to confirm with Legal)
- SRE: investigate root cause for 11/01 tail latency spike (initial hypothesis: burst scheduling + degraded NVLink throughput) — detailed postmortem requested.

Notes on tone & coordination:
- Meeting consensus was to be conservative during the serving-runtime kernel change window to avoid noisy rollbacks. Teams should focus on test coverage, telemetry, and small phased rollouts over fast-but-broad rollout.
- Leadership emphasized communicating the temporary freeze and capacity decisions clearly to CS & Solutions Engineering to set customer expectations.

Next meeting: weekly interlock on 2026-11-10 at 09:30 PT. Requested pre-reads: latest autoscaler perf runbook (JIRA-4482 notes), kernel PR perf summary, and compliance artifact checklist draft.

Appendix: quick links referenced in discussion: JIRA-4482 (autoscaler), JIRA-4710 (capacity planning), PR #987 (kernel grouped-attention), confluence roadmap page (linked above).

End of notes.
